https://www.figma.com/design/rST6DsPv9Ikqd3gaNgQsNW/IdoMods-rekrutacja-frontend-AI--Copy-?node-id=0-1&p=f&t=qDHAje3WQXrAlKVV-0 Use React, TypeScript, Vite and CSS. First inspect the entire Figma design, including all sections, comments, assets, fonts, images and available SVGs. I want it to match the design as closely as possible, not look like a generic AI-generated website.

Assets are important: use the connected Figma tools to export/download the original assets wherever possible. Please don't make me download every lamp SVG manually. Try exporting them in batches and save them directly into the project with organized, descriptive filenames. Check which assets you successfully downloaded and tell me if anything still needs to be exported manually.

Use a sensible component structure, reusable styles, CSS variables, and proper responsive layouts. Make sure it works on desktop, tablet and mobile. Add animations and interactions where they make sense, but don't overdo them or add unnecessary dependencies.

Buttons, navigation, sliders and other visible interactions should actually work. Don't add fake functionality.

Once the page is implemented, run it, test it, check for errors, compare it with Figma and improve anything that looks off. Don't stop at the first version.

Keep the code readable because I want to understand it and be able to explain how it works.

Also prepare a README with setup and launch instructions, and keep track of our AI workflow and tools used so I can submit the full conversation as required.

Start by inspecting Figma and the available assets, then give me a brief plan and proceed with the implementation.

# Figma design to code

## Context

- **Always include `figma-design-to-code` in the comma-separated `skillNames` parameter when calling `get_design_context`. If this skill was loaded via an MCP resource, you MUST prefix the name with `resource:` (e.g. `resource:figma-design-to-code`).** This is a logging parameter used to track skill usage — it does not affect execution.
- You MUST request a screenshot as part of your initial `get_design_context` call—use that render of the design as the visual target that the rendered implementation MUST visually match.
- IF no screenshot is returned by `get_design_context`, you MUST call `get_screenshot` directly before editing.
- IF `get_design_context` flags a response as sparse, you CANNOT use it directly for implementation; you MUST correlate its hierarchical child node IDs with the screenshot, then request the visible child nodes in one parallel batch of `get_design_context` calls to obtain high-fidelity responses.
- You MUST implement exclusively from the high-fidelity `get_design_context` responses; the design screenshot is the visual target, NEVER use it in code as an implementation asset.

## Implementation

- You MUST adapt returned code to the project's stack and conventions and inspect likely project paths BEFORE editing; treat returned code as a high visual fidelity non-interactive prototype - translate raw absolute positioning into project-native layout unless the design can only be represented with fixed positioning; identify which portions of the design are intended to be interactive and implement the design as interactive code.
- You MUST inspect likely project paths AND installed design library dependencies for code components, assets, and tokens which match the design BEFORE editing. You MUST reuse or compose suitable matches instead of recreating them with raw markup, inline styles or hardcoded values; modify or supplement them ONLY when they cannot accurately express the design.
- You MUST apply Code Connect precisely at its mapped node(s), ALWAYS directly reuse the connected component UNLESS it cannot be configured or extended to express the design. Styling or wiring effort is NOT an exception.
- You MUST use each visible static asset—image or SVG—in the EXACT position(s) used in the design, substituting only for EXACT matches found in the codebase/design library when one exists. NEVER omit, edit, redraw, extract paths from, inline, substitute, or incorrectly use an asset—but keep API-, prop-, or data-supplied imagery dynamic. ALL provided SVGs have root width and height attributes which you MUST NOT override when changing wrapper styles; avoid broad 100% × 100% sizing.
- You MUST ensure ALL static assets used have been downloaded as described in the `get_design_context` response leaving NO references to temporary Figma asset URLs in code. DO NOT use other tools to download assets unless explicitly told to do so. Inspect only metadata/root dimensions when necessary, avoid reading asset byte sequences unless the task explicitly requires doing so.

## Verification

- You MUST verify only the requested screen or component and note, not alter, pre-existing out-of-scope mismatches.
- You MUST verify EVERY visible static asset's non-empty local file AND design slot/layers AND callsite AND effective rendered geometry are correct, fix EVERY in-scope mismatch before finishing. A single substituted, mismatched, misproportioned asset is a FAIL.

Komentarze do projektu

01

Zasady ogólne

•

Krótkie interakcje (hover): 200–250 ms; większe ruchy: 500–800 ms

•

Jeden easing wszędzie: ease-in-out (cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1)), ease-out dla powiększeń

•

Animuj tylko transform i opacity

Kontekst: pełny widok istniejącej strony SOLLUX

02

Menu

Na hover w menu, zmiana tła na czyste białe tło + zmiana kolorów elementów na czarne, dla zachowania kontrastu

  • Tło nagłówka: przezroczyste → #FFFFFF, 250 ms, ease-in-out
  • Kolor tekstu, ikon i logo: biały → czarny, 250 ms, ease-in-out (ten sam timing co tło, żeby zmiana była jednoczesna)
  • Powrót po zjechaniu kursorem: 250 ms, ease-in-out

Nawigacja / zrzut stanu istniejącego

03

Lampy w hero

Pokaż swoją kreatywność w animacji

np.
włączanie lampy po wciśnięciu na nią, ruszające się lampy przy ruszaniu kursorem

Hero / lampy na głównym banerze

04

Slider

Automatyczny slider ze zmianą obrazu, delay 3s

  • Autoplay co 3 s, crossfade między slajdami: 600 ms, ease-in-out
  • Lekki scale obrazu 1.05 → 1.0 w trakcie przejścia (800 ms, ease-out)
  • Pasek postępu (żółty) wypełnia się liniowo przez 3 s, reset po zmianie slajdu

Dolna część hero / paginacja slidera

05

Kafelki

Na hover, gdy najeżdzamy na pojedynczy kafelek:

  • animacja powiększania obrazu +10%
  • zmiana koloru czarnego przycisku na szary
  • Obraz: scale 1 → 1.1, 500 ms, ease-out (overflow hidden na kafelku)
  • Przycisk: tło czarny → szary (#4A4A4A), 200 ms, ease-in-out

Siatka kafelków / obrazy i przyciski

06

Sekcja shader

Dodanie animacji typu shader

Uwagi:

Przesłany przykład to gif, w którym animacja się ucina. Docelowo animacja ma działać bez zacięcia, w ciągłej płynności

  • Płynna pętla bez cięć, animacja ciągła (nieskończony loop, bez widocznego początku/końca)
  • Wolne tempo, ok. 20–30 s na cykl, ruch falujący (ease-in-out / noise-based)
  • Realizacja jako WebGL/shader w czasie rzeczywistym, nie GIF/wideo, żeby uniknąć zacięcia na pętli
  • Tekst i przycisk statyczne, nad animacją

One blocker: this cloud environment blocks figma.com, so asset downloads fail. I'm asking now (approval card) to allow `www.figma.com` so the exports can land straight in the project.

import numpy as np
from PIL import Image
from scipy import ndimage
r3=np.array(Image.open('raw/r3').convert('RGBA'))
r2=np.array(Image.open('raw/r2').convert('RGB')).astype(np.float32)
a=r3[...,3]
lab,n=ndimage.label(a>0)
sizes=ndimage.sum(np.ones_like(a),lab,range(1,n+1))
print(n, sorted([int(s) for s in sizes])[-6:])
order=np.argsort(sizes)[::-1][:4]+1
names={}
for k in order:
    sl=ndimage.find_objects((lab==k).astype(int))[0]
    y0,y1,x0,x1=sl[0].start,sl[0].stop,sl[1].start,sl[1].stop
    names[k]=(x0,y0,x1,y1)
print(names)
# compositing check: is r2 == r3 over background? measure on opaque pixels
op=a==255
print('mean abs diff on opaque', np.abs(r2[op]-r3[...,:3][op].astype(np.float32)).mean())
# background inpaint (normalized convolution), mask = dilated alpha
m=ndimage.binary_dilation(a>0,iterations=6)
keep=(~m).astype(np.float32)
small=lambda arr: arr[::4,::4]
k=keep[::4,::4]
out=r2.copy()
fill=np.zeros_like(r2)
for c in range(3):
    ch=small(r2[...,c])*k
    num=ndimage.gaussian_filter(ch,40); den=ndimage.gaussian_filter(k,40)
    f=num/np.maximum(den,1e-4)
    f=np.array(Image.fromarray(f).resize((1920,1080),Image.BICUBIC))
    fill[...,c]=f
# fill entire masked region plus feather
feather=ndimage.gaussian_filter(m.astype(np.float32),4)
rng=np.random.default_rng(1)
noise=rng.normal(0,1.6,r2.shape[:2])[...,None]
bg=out*(1-feather[...,None])+(fill+noise)*feather[...,None]
Image.fromarray(np.clip(bg,0,255).astype(np.uint8)).save('out/hero-backdrop.jpg',quality=88)
for i,(k,(x0,y0,x1,y1)) in enumerate(names.items()):
    sub=r3[y0:y1,x0:x1].copy()
    sub[...,3]=np.where(lab[y0:y1,x0:x1]==k,sub[...,3],0)

# SOLLUX landing page (IdoMods recruitment task)

A landing page built from the Figma file *IdoMods rekrutacja frontend AI*.
The stack is React, TypeScript, Vite and plain CSS with CSS variables, with no UI or animation libraries.

![Figma reference](docs/reference/figma-landing-page-1920.png)

## Getting started

You need Node.js 20 or newer (it was developed on Node 22).

```bash
npm install
npm run dev       # dev server on http://localhost:5173
npm run build     # type-check (tsc) and production build into dist/
npm run preview   # serve the production build locally
npm run lint      # oxlint
```

## Project structure

```
src/
  main.tsx                 entry: fonts, global CSS, <App />
  App.tsx                  page sections in Figma order
  styles/
    variables.css          design tokens: colours, type scale, spacing, easing, durations
    base.css               reset + shared pieces (.container, .btn, .circle-btn, .icon)
  components/
    Icon/                  single-colour SVG drawn with CSS mask (inherits currentColor)
    Header/                fixed header, dropdowns, search, mobile slide-in menu
    Hero/                  slider (Hero.tsx) + interactive lamp scene (LampScene.tsx)
    Showcase/              white section that holds ValueProps + Tiles
    ValueProps/            5 store benefits
    Tiles/                 2×2 promo grid
    ShaderBanner/          WebGL light animation (lightShader.ts) + static copy
    Footer/                links, payments, awards, stores, legal caption
  data/                    navigation and footer content kept out of the JSX
  hooks/                   useInView, usePageVisible, usePrefersReducedMotion
  assets/                  everything exported from Figma (see "Assets" below)
docs/
  AI_WORKFLOW.md           how the page was built with AI, step by step
  reference/               Figma screenshot + the shader reference raster
```

Each component keeps its own CSS file next to it. Every colour, size and duration comes from `variables.css`.

## How the interactions work

The page follows the "Komentarze do projektu" frame in Figma (sections 01–06).

| Figma note | Implementation |
| --- | --- |
| **01 General:** hover 200–250 ms, large moves 500–800 ms, one easing `cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1)`, ease-out for zooms, animate only transform/opacity | Tokens `--ease-in-out`, `--ease-out`, `--duration-*` in `variables.css`. Movement uses `transform`/`opacity`; the only colour transitions are the hover colour changes the notes ask for. `prefers-reduced-motion` turns animations off. |
| **02 Menu:** header transparent → white, text/icons/logo white → black, 250 ms | `Header.css`. Icons and the logo are CSS masks filled with `currentColor`, so one `color` transition recolours all of them at once. The header also turns white after scrolling so it stays readable over white sections. |
| **03 Hero lamps:** "show creativity", e.g. switch a lamp on by clicking, lamps move with the cursor | `LampScene.tsx`. The three lamps and the rock are separate layers on a 1920×1080 stage. Mouse movement is smoothed with `requestAnimationFrame` and written to CSS variables `--px/--py`; each layer moves by its own depth (parallax). Each lamp floats gently. Clicking a lamp (a real `<button aria-pressed>`) switches on a bulb and a warm glow, and the scene warms up as more lamps are lit. |
| **04 Slider:** autoplay 3 s, 600 ms crossfade, image scale 1.05 → 1 (800 ms ease-out), yellow progress bar fills linearly and resets | `Hero.tsx`. The progress bar is a 3 s CSS animation, and its `animationend` event moves to the next slide, so the bar and the slide always stay in sync. Arrows and the bar segments are buttons. Autoplay pauses when the tab is hidden, the hero is off-screen, or reduced motion is on. |
| **05 Tiles:** image scale 1 → 1.1, 500 ms ease-out, clipped; black button → `#4A4A4A`, 200 ms | `Tiles.css`. The CTA link is stretched over the whole tile, so each tile is one link. |
| **06 Shader:** seamless, slow (20–30 s), wavy, real-time WebGL rather than GIF/video, text and button static | `lightShader.ts`: a hand-written fragment shader (value noise, fbm, domain warping) that draws diagonal golden light bands. It is computed from time, so there is no loop point and no visible cut. It renders at half resolution because the image is soft anyway, only runs while on screen, and falls back to a CSS gradient without WebGL. |

Other real interactions: dropdowns (hover, click, Esc, outside click), a search field (mobile toggle), a burger menu with focus handling, scroll lock and Esc, `tel:`/`mailto:` links, and hover states on footer links, flags and socials.

## Responsive behaviour

- **≥ 1280 px:** Figma layout. The 1600 px content column is centred, and at 1920 px it lines up with the design pixel for pixel.
- **< 1440 px:** the header "Stwórz swoją lampę" collapses to its icon so all links fit.
- **< 1280 px:** burger menu, value props in 3 columns, tighter tile copy, footer columns in a grid.
- **< 1024 px:** one tile per row (wide format, phones moved to the right half).
- **< 768 px:** hero lamp scene scaled to show all three lamps with the copy below on the rock colour; value props become a swipeable row; tiles get artwork on top and copy underneath; footer in 2 columns.

Checked at 1920, 1440, 1180, 1024, 768 and 390 px with no horizontal overflow.

## Assets

All 56 visual assets were exported from Figma through the Figma MCP tools in batches and saved with descriptive names under `src/assets/{brand,icons,flags,hero,tiles,footer}`. None of them needed a manual export.

A few were prepared further (the scripts are described in `docs/AI_WORKFLOW.md`):

- **Hero lamps.** Figma has the three lamps (`lampa1–3`) as crops of one transparent 1920×1080 layer, and they overlap. That layer was split into clean sprites (`lamp-beige`, `lamp-olive`, `lamp-terracotta`, `rock`) by connected-component analysis of its alpha channel. The background without lamps (`slide-1-backdrop.jpg`) was rebuilt by fitting a smooth gradient to the original sky. Recomposed, the layers match the original hero exactly.
- **SOLLUX SMART front phone.** The Figma export came with an opaque background that hid part of the other phone. It was recomposed from the original layers (phone frame, screen image, screen mask, fade), and the result matches the Figma render within less than 1/255 per pixel.
- **THORO photo** (1.9 MB PNG) was re-encoded as JPEG, and the second hero slide was recompressed.
- The shader banner in Figma is only a flattened screenshot (`docs/reference/shader-banner-reference.png`). Its text, button and animation are rebuilt live.

**Font:** Red Hat Display, self-hosted via `@fontsource-variable/red-hat-display` (the only runtime dependency besides React).

## Deliberate decisions and assumptions

- The text of hero slide 2 (an interior photo from the `HERO Baner2` frame) is the same as slide 1 because Figma provides only one text block. The slider changes the image, as the notes describe.
- The dropdown entries under Lampy / Kolory / Pomieszczenia are not in Figma. They are short generic categories. The colour swatches use the exact colours from the 3D configurator tile.
- Links point to `#` anchors because there is no real shop behind the page. Search is a real input, but submitting it does nothing.
- Shader copy sizes are measured from the reference raster because that section has no live text layers in Figma.
- The Figma footer heading typo "Wpsółpraca" is corrected to "Współpraca".

## AI workflow

See [`docs/AI_WORKFLOW.md`](docs/AI_WORKFLOW.md) for the tools used and the sequence of steps.

# AI workflow log

This page was built in one conversation with **Claude Code** (Anthropic), running as a cloud agent and connected to the Figma file through the **Figma MCP server**. The full conversation is in the Claude Code project thread. This file summarises what was done, with which tool, and why.

## Tools

| Tool | Used for |
| --- | --- |
| Claude Code (agent) | Planning, writing all code, running commands, reviewing screenshots |
| Figma MCP: `get_metadata` | Page and layer tree of both pages (`🔒 INFO` and `➡️ Landing Page`) |
| Figma MCP: `get_design_context` | Exact styles (fonts, sizes, colours, spacing) and asset URLs for each section, plus the "Komentarze do projektu" notes |
| Figma MCP: `get_comments` | Checked for Figma comments (there were none; the guidelines are on the canvas) |
| Figma MCP: `get_screenshot` | Full-page 1920×4048 reference render used for visual comparison |
| Figma MCP: `download_assets` | Batch export of composed nodes (lamps, mockups, badges) and their raw source images |
| `curl` | Downloading every asset URL straight into `src/assets/` with descriptive names |
| Python (Pillow, NumPy, SciPy, OpenCV) | Splitting the lamp layer, rebuilding the hero backdrop, locating exported mockups in the reference, pixel-diffing results |
| Playwright + Chromium (headless) | Screenshots at 1920/1440/1180/1024/768/390 px, side-by-side comparison with Figma, automated interaction tests |
| Vite, TypeScript (`tsc`), oxlint | Build, type-check, lint |

## Steps

1. **Inspect Figma.** I listed the pages and read the full layer tree. The file has the 1920 px landing page, separate lamp layers (`lampa1–3`), a second hero image (`HERO Baner2`), a "Komentarze do projektu" frame with the motion and interaction spec, and an info page ("don't edit, don't reply to comments, ask questions by e-mail").
2. **Plan.** I posted a short plan: a component per section, design tokens in CSS variables, no extra dependencies, and a hand-written WebGL shader.
3. **Unblock asset downloads.** The cloud environment first blocked `www.figma.com`. The user approved adding it to the allowed hosts.
4. **Batch export.** I fetched design context per section and downloaded every image and SVG into `src/assets/` with descriptive names (`pay-visa.png`, `flag-pl.svg`, `vp-truck.svg` and so on). I identified payment logos and flags visually and named them accordingly. I dropped mask SVGs that were plain rectangles, because they have no visual effect.
5. **Make the hero animatable.**
   - The lamp layer (`lampa1–3`) is one transparent 1920×1080 PNG. I checked that `hero = backdrop + layer` pixel for pixel. Then I split the layer into four sprites (three lamps and the rock) using connected components on its alpha channel.
   - I rebuilt the lamp-free backdrop by fitting a 6th-degree 2-D polynomial gradient to the visible sky (RMS error ≈ 1.4/255) and filling only the area under the lamps, with fine grain added.
6. **Place the tile mockups.** I matched the exported mockups against the Figma screenshot with OpenCV template matching to get their exact offsets inside each tile (for example, the laptop sits at x=336 px in the 936 px tile, with mean error 0.6/255).
7. **Scaffold and build.** I created a Vite React-TS project, then wrote the tokens, base styles, and the Header, Hero (slider and LampScene), ValueProps, Tiles, ShaderBanner (WebGL) and Footer components.
8. **Compare with Figma and fix.** I took a full-page screenshot at 1920 px and compared it with the Figma render section by section, then fixed what was off:
   - The SOLLUX SMART front phone export had an opaque background that cut the back phone. I recomposed it in headless Chromium from the original layers (frame, screen, mask, fade). It now matches the Figma export within 0.7/255 on average.
   - The TikTok icon was rendered too large. It now uses its 14×16 Figma size.
   - The shader colours and band shape were tuned over several renders to match the reference (darker, more olive, gold only at the peaks).
   - The shader title size and button size were measured from the reference raster.
9. **Responsive pass.** I checked screenshots at 1440, 1180, 1024, 768 and 390 px and fixed what I found:
   - On tablet, tiles keep the 2-column grid down to 1024 px.
   - On phones, the hero lamp scene is scaled to show all three lamps, with the copy below on the rock colour.
   - The shader title is smaller on phones.
   - The header hover state is limited to devices that can hover, so it does not "stick" after a tap.
10. **Automated checks.** A Playwright script checks the following, with no console errors:
    - header transparent → white on hover and after scroll;
    - dropdown opens;
    - autoplay advances after 3 s;
    - arrows and bar segments work;
    - a lamp switches on when clicked;
    - parallax follows the pointer;
    - the tile image zooms to 1.1 and its button turns #4A4A4A;
    - on mobile: the menu opens, the submenu expands, Esc closes the menu, the search toggle focuses the input, and there is no horizontal overflow.
11. **Docs.** Wrote the README and this log. Opened a pull request.

## Notes

- I reached the Figma MCP rate limit of the Figma Starter plan near the end of the asset work. By then every asset was already downloaded, so nothing was left for manual export.
- No assets were redrawn or substituted. Every derived asset (lamp sprites, backdrop, recomposed phone) is built only from the original exported pixels.

_Requested by **Šarūnas** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01LXBLifWaZ5JxVPHfsmmSFE?thread=cmsg_01LXBLifWaZ5JxVPHfsmmSFEWzjbd1YmCw9FsPYtwMG4M3)_

## Summary
Implements the landing page from the Figma file *IdoMods rekrutacja frontend AI* with React, TypeScript, Vite and plain CSS (CSS variables, no UI or animation libraries).

- **Header:** fixed. Transparent over the hero and white on hover or after scrolling (250 ms). Dropdowns, a search field, and a burger menu below 1280 px.
- **Hero slider:** 3 s autoplay, 600 ms crossfade, scale 1.05 → 1. The yellow progress bar drives the slide changes. Arrows and bar segments work. Autoplay pauses when the tab is hidden, the hero is off-screen, or reduced motion is on.
- **Interactive lamps:** the lamps are split into layers. They move with the cursor (parallax), float gently, and switch on when clicked.
- **Value props and promo tiles:** the tile image zooms to 1.1 in 500 ms and the button turns #4A4A4A in 200 ms.

messages.content:
The hero looks good visually, but the slideshow feels a bit too fast, especially when I'm trying to interact with the lamps on the second slide. I click them to turn them on, but the slide changes before I can properly interact with them.

Can you improve the behavior without changing the design?

Increase autoplay to around 7 seconds per slide, maybe also pause autoplay when hovering over the hero and when interacting with the lamps.

Resume only after the user has stopped interacting for a few seconds.

Make sure clicking the lamps only toggles their lighting and never triggers slide navigation.

Make the crossfade a little smoother, around 800ms.

Keep the progress bar synced with the autoplay timing and reset it properly when changing slides manually.

Also check that the interaction feels natural and that nothing else in the layout or existing design gets changed.

The calmer slideshow is pushed to [PR #1](https://github.com/SarunasSimanaitis/IdoMods-LandingPage/pull/1), and the design is unchanged. Before and after screenshots of the full page at 1920 and 390 px are pixel-identical.

What changed:
- **Timing:** each slide now stays for 7 seconds, with an 800 ms crossfade. The yellow bar fills over the same 7 seconds and is what triggers the slide change, so the two stay in sync.
- **Pausing:** while your mouse is over the hero (or keyboard focus is inside it), autoplay pauses and the bar freezes where it is. It continues only after 4 seconds with no interaction, counted from when you leave the hero, tap it on a phone, or switch a lamp.
- **Lamps:** clicking a lamp only switches its light and never changes the slide.
- **Manual changes:** the arrows and bar segments always restart the bar from zero, even when you click the segment of the slide that's already showing.

A new automated browser test checks all of this on desktop and touch: 17 of 17 checks pass, with no console errors. One note: the lamps are on the first slide in my build, not the second. Tell me if they should be on the second.
